title: Optimum adaptation of a Steiner network
summary: The Euclidean Steiner tree problem, normally posed in two dimensions, seeks to connect a set of prescribed terminal nodes by placing additional nodes, known as Steiner points, with edges connecting such nodes either to another Steiner point or a terminal node, and with the placements minimising the sum of all the edge lengths of the associated tree. We consider a problem in which we start with a known solution to a Steiner tree problem, and the terminal positions are then perturbed.
